name: Stage 1 weighted overlay
weights_status: illustrative — not calibrated against flood records

terms.label: Height above nearest drainage
terms.why: Water from an overflowing channel reaches ground that sits only a few metres above it (HAND < 5 m is the usual flood-prone band).

terms.label: Distance to river or canal
terms.why: Riverine flooding spreads out from mapped channels.

terms.label: Flatness
terms.why: On flat ground water spreads and lingers instead of draining away.

terms.label: Elevation above sea level
terms.why: Low coastal and valley-floor land is where rivers back up, especially at high tide.

terms.label: Observed surface-water history
terms.why: Places satellites have seen under water before (1984–2021) tend to be wet again.

scenarios.label: Heavy
scenarios.note: Class thresholds lowered by 0.05 — more ground flagged.

scenarios.label: Extreme
scenarios.note: Thresholds lowered by 0.10. Hypothetical stress test, not an observed event.
